fact: ITWeb Africa states the National Cybersecurity Committee is the main strategic and advisory body for protecting Mauritius against digital threats and managing national cyber resilience, with legal authority to enforce compliance alongside law enforcement.

L'Express reports the Cabinet noted promulgation of the CII Designation Regulations 2026, which empower the National Cybersecurity Committee to designate a system as critical information infrastructure under the Cybersecurity and Cybercrime Act.
The SADC statement of 13 September 2018 says Mauritius has an established and operational national CIRT.
The ICT minister refers to the Computer Emergency Response Team of Mauritius (CERT-MU) as an existing body that is to sign a content takedown agreement with Meta.

CERT-MU published a security bulletin on 22 October 2026 rating the PHP2Shell vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-109618 and -109619) critical at 9.2, and the government took some state sites offline as a precaution.
The National Cyber Security Committee was immediately seized of the PHP2shell vulnerability, and the government took about 70% of its sites offline on its recommendation, per ICT minister Ramtohul.

The Acting Prime Minister cited figures published by the Mauritius Digital Promotion Agency, based on data from the ICT Authority and CERT-MU, showing reported security incidents rose from 5,221 in 2024 to 6,073 in 2025.

The gazetted regulations refer to the National Cybersecurity Committee established under section 3 of the Cybersecurity and Cybercrime Act 2021, which may designate critical information infrastructure.

The National Audit Office report, as reported by l'express, says the National Cybersecurity Committee is a body provided for by law and that CERTMU operates under the ministry, though the committee was not operational by end 2025.
Le Mauricien reports, citing MAUCORS+ (run by CERT-MU), 47 phishing cases reported in 2025.
Mauritius's Prime Minister told Parliament that CERT-MU, under the ministry of ICT, runs MAUCORS+, the national platform for reporting cybersecurity incidents and online offences.
